presentation.label: PLAYHEAD DIRECTION
presentation.summary: Play patterns reversed, pingpong, random or shuffled: per pattern, shared by every track or set per track.
presentation.overview: Play Modes changes which step the sequencer plays at each position: NORMAL, REVERSED, PINGPONG (end steps once), PINGPONG 2 (end steps twice), RANDOM or SHUFFLE. Each pattern keeps its own modes: one shared mode under SCALE MODE NORMAL, one per audio and MIDI track under PER TRACK. Trigs, conditions, micro-timing, swing and locks move with their step; tempo, lengths, chains and the trig LEDs stay in step. The modes are saved with the project, survive a power cycle and follow pattern copy, paste and clear.
highlights: Six playhead modes, including two pingpongs and a shuffle that plays every step once per pass
Per pattern; per track under PER TRACK scale mode, audio and MIDI tracks
Hold a TRACK key and press UP or DOWN; a popup names the mode
Saved in the project, kept over a power cycle, carried by pattern copy and paste
usage: Hold a TRACK key and press DOWN to step through NORMAL, REVERSED, PINGPONG, PINGPONG 2, RANDOM and SHUFFLE; UP walks back. The popup shows ALL <mode> under SCALE MODE NORMAL, or T1..T8 / M1..M8 <mode> under PER TRACK.
Each pattern keeps its own modes; PLAY and every pattern change start the tracks from their first step again.
Under PER TRACK, MASTER LENGTH limits how far a track gets; set it to INF to let every track run its full length in every mode.

access.location: Automatic when included in a build: hold a TRACK key on the main screen and press UP or DOWN.
steps: Include Play Modes in your build. It uses no effect slot and no knob.
Load a pattern and choose its SCALE MODE in PATTERN SETTINGS: NORMAL for one shared mode, PER TRACK for one mode per track.
Hold TRACK 1 (or the track to change) and press DOWN or UP; the popup shows the new mode. Press PLAY.
Hold the TRACK key and press UP until the popup shows NORMAL to return to stock playback.

limitations: Does not combine with octabam's PLOCKS P2 (not in this catalog): both use battery RAM 0x100f8600.. and the 20 pattern-copy memcpy sites.
Deliberate stock-flow change: TRACK held + UP / DOWN changes the mode and does not reach the stock arrow handler; project.work gains #PLAY_MODES= comment lines.
Copying a single track does not copy its mode; PROJECT > NEW may keep the previous project's modes (untested).
Played interactively on one MKII (builds 12-24); MKI, micro-timing, trig conditions, slides, live recording and MIDI tracks beyond a first check are untested.
Chip worst-case cycles are unmeasured; no stress project has been run.
Like every DRAM module, the build gives up about 10 MB of sample memory to the platform reserve.
Build-24 physical reboot, Part/project save-reload after later edits and distinct-track isolation were not rechecked; build-19 persistence results remain historical.

resources.recorded: 8 October 2026: emulator counts and build memory (build 24); chip timing unmeasured

storage.label: DRAM data + battery RAM
storage.display: 14,876 B: 12,566 B unit in DRAM + 2,310 B battery RAM
storage.conditions: Code 7,700, read-only data 102, state and pattern table 4,764 (SDRAM platform reserve), battery table 2,310 (CS1). All shared; stack at most 120 bytes. See evidence/memory.md.

processing.label: ColdFire processing
processing.conditions: Instruction counts of the module's own code in octabam's ColdFire core, no firmware, synthetic sequencer state; SHUFFLE's walk bounded analytically. Chip cycles: 32-cycle-per-instruction allowance, not measured.

impact.conditions: 16 tracks (8 audio, 8 MIDI) in SHUFFLE, the most expensive mode, at the highest tempo and finest track scale; a project load rewriting the battery table.

cpu.rationale: Per track per step a few byte reads, one pass test and one mapping; SHUFFLE adds a keyed permutation (about two evaluations, three multiplies each). Battery-RAM writes only on key presses, pattern copies and project loads.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code, tables or buffers; stock DSP processing is unchanged.

memory.rationale: About 4.7 KB of DRAM data in the platform reserve plus the unit's code, and a 2,310-byte battery-RAM table; no per-instance copies.

tests.summary: Host suites for the engine and firmware glue pass; instruction counts in octabam's ColdFire core bound one track step at 4,654 instructions (1,884 measured); the author ran builds 12–24 on an MKII (functional report). No stress run, no chip timing.

conditions.parameterExtremes: Every mode, track lengths 1–64, MASTER LENGTH INF and 0, all seven track scales across the 16 tracks.
conditions.parameterModulation: No knob, LFO or p-lock reaches the module; mode changes by TRACK + UP / DOWN measured separately (674 instructions). Scenes, LFOs and locks are stock and unchanged.
conditions.modeSwitching: Every mode and both scale modes, with a PLAY restart on every run; pattern-row reloads on pattern switches included. MASTER LENGTH restarts (14-step tracks under master 16) measured in every mode.
conditions.maxLoad: All 16 tracks (8 audio, 8 MIDI) in one step, SHUFFLE at the longest walk (length 33), every track restarting: bounded at 74,464 instructions; budget one step at 300 BPM, 2X scale, 264 MHz.
conditions.inputConditions: No audio path. 60 SHUFFLE seeds per length; the walk length bound (32) from the permutation's construction, its cost measured as 101 + 98 × walk.

regions.name: Code: C engine and glue, 35 detour stubs and entries
Read-only data: mode names, project key, tables
State, flags, popup text, project line, computed track lengths and the 256-pattern mode table

memory.conditions: From the build-24 runtime ELF and the battery layout; one table for all tracks and patterns, no per-track copies; stack at most 120 bytes below the caller (measured); no heap, DSP memory or cave space. The platform reserve's 10 MB is shared by every DRAM module.

hardware.summary: On an Octatrack MKII the author ran builds 12–19 (3–7 Oct; build 19 for about 15 minutes: PINGPONG 2, per-pattern modes, save and reload, a power cycle, pattern copy and paste also to other banks, clear pattern) and builds 20–24 (this source, 8 Oct), which fix length mismatches after switching NORMAL to PER TRACK and under MASTER LENGTH, restart PINGPONG at each master loop (also for a 15-step track under master 16, checked by ear) and keep the trig LEDs on the played step there.
limitations: A short interactive report, not a timed stress run; no audio or timing measurement.
Micro-timing, trig conditions, slides, live recording, scenes and Parts during non-NORMAL playback, and MIDI tracks beyond a first check were not tested.
No combination with other modules on the unit.
Build-24 physical reboot, Part/project save-reload after later edits and distinct-track isolation were not rechecked; build-19 persistence results remain historical.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Include Play Modes in your build and load a pattern with a trig on step 1 only; SCALE MODE NORMAL.
Hold TRACK 1, press DOWN once: ALL REVERSED. Press PLAY: the trig sounds on the last step of every bar, and the trig LEDs walk 16 → 1.
Hold TRACK 1, press DOWN twice more: ALL PINGPONG 2: the trig sounds twice in a row at every turn back to step 1. Hold TRACK 1 and press UP until ALL NORMAL to return to stock playback.
